cards.text: Jesus, God's Son, just finished telling a story about a nobleman who goes away to become king. Now He goes on ahead, going up to Jerusalem. Near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sends out two of His disciples.

cards.question: Jesus sends two disciples into the village ahead. What does He say they'll find tied up there?
Jesus tells the two disciples that no one has ever sat on this colt.

cards.text: Jesus tells them to untie it and bring it to Him. He even gets them ready for the awkward moment when somebody asks, “Why are you untying it?”

cards.question: If anyone asks the two disciples why they're untying the colt, what does Jesus tell them to say?

answers.text: We will bring it back soon

cards.text: So the two head out, and they find it just as Jesus had told them. Friend, I once got lost inside a DRAWER, and these two walk straight to it in a whole village.

cards.question: As the disciples are untying the colt, its ___ ask them why they're untying it.
When the owners ask why, the two disciples answer with the line Jesus gave them: The Lord needs it.

cards.text: They lead the colt to Jesus, throw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it. No saddle? No problem, friend, those cloaks just got PROMOTED.

cards.question: As Jesus rides along on the colt, what do the people spread on the road?

cards.text: Jesus reaches the road going down from the Mount of Olives, and the whole multitude of disciples starts praising God joyfully in a loud voice. And I mean LOUD, friend, like a stadium when the home team scores.

cards.question: The whole crowd of disciples is praising God joyfully on the road down from the Mount of Olives. What are they praising Him for?

answers.text: All the miracles they had seen

cards.question: As they praise God, what do the disciples call the One who comes in the name of the Lord?

cards.text: They shout, “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!” But some of the Pharisees, a group of strict religious teachers, are in the crowd, and they've got a request for Jesus.

cards.question: Some Pharisees in the crowd call Jesus Teacher and ask Him to ___ His disciples.

cards.text: Jesus doesn't hush the crowd. He answers the Pharisees right there in the middle of all that noise, and friend, it's an answer.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if His disciples remain silent, something else will cry out. What is it?

cards.text: All that praise on the road, and now Jesus comes near Jerusalem. He sees the city.

cards.question: As Jesus approaches Jerusalem and sees the city, what does He do?

answers.text: He sings a psalm over it
He blesses it with a shout

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace!” The crowd is shouting about peace in heaven, and Jesus is talking about the peace this city missed.

cards.question: Jesus says that what would bring Jerusalem peace is now hidden from its eyes.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks ahead. He says the days will come when the city's enemies will barricade it, surround it and hem it in on every side.

cards.question: Jesus says the enemies will level the city to the ground and will not leave one ___ on another.
Why does Jesus say all this will come on Jerusalem?

answers.text: It did not recognize God's visit
It did not keep the Sabbath
It made peace with its enemies

findings.problem: The card states a Bible fact from outside the passage: Jesus just finished telling a story about a nobleman who goes away to become king (Luke 19:11-27). The card's citation is only Luke 19:28-29, so this fact has no reference.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card tells Jesus' instruction to untie the colt and bring it, which is in Luke 19:30. The card cites only Luke 19:31. The citation should be Luke 19:30-31.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't share the fact's core action. The disciples find the colt just as Jesus said. Getting lost inside a drawer is a different action, so the contrast doesn't click right away. The phrase 'walk straight to it' also adds a detail the text doesn't give, since Luke 19:32 only says they found it just as Jesus had told them.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus 'reaches the road going down from the Mount of Olives'. Luke 19:37 says He 'approached the descent'. The card stretches the text.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card's voice is flat ('and friend, it's an answer'). This is the setup for one of the passage's biggest lines, and it holds no real laugh or energy.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact wording of the phrase 'not leave one stone on another', which they haven't seen. The wrong answer 'beam' fits the meaning of a city leveled to the ground just as well, so the card tests wording, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
